common_name: Orange Smoothie Daylily (Rainbow Rhythm Orange Mango Rebloomer)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this Walters Gardens Rainbow Rhythm introduction (US Plant Patent PP28643) rewards generous spacing and consistent moisture with heavy rebloom.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Orange Smoothie bears fragrant, diamond-dusted orange-mango flowers about four inches across with a light rose band, pink midrib, and green throat, carried on well-branched scapes loaded with roughly 30 buds. A dependable rebloomer that begins in early midseason and continues flowering well into late summer, it is drought-tolerant once established and rabbit resistant. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.

common_name: Blazing Glory Daylily (Golden Rebloomer with Burgundy Picotee Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; this tetraploid Rainbow Rhythm introduction from Walters Gardens blooms heaviest with consistent moisture.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to part shade; Blazing Glory produces fragrant, six-inch golden yellow flowers with a bold burgundy-red eye and a matching picotee edge that holds its crisp margin rather than bleeding into the petal. This tetraploid rebloomer carries semi-evergreen foliage and flowers in midseason with a strong second flush. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and flower size.

common_name: American Revolution Daylily (Velvety Dark Wine-Red Self)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; this vigorous 1972 Gilbert H. Wild introduction increases quickly into substantial clumps.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; American Revolution bears older-style, narrow-petaled flowers of velvety deep wine-red with a yellow throat and small green heart, on scapes reaching about 28 inches. Introduced by Gilbert H. Wild in 1972 and later given an AHS Honorable Mention, it is a fast increaser that reblooms and remains a dependable garden workhorse. Divide crowded clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor.
sources: Gilbert H. Wild & Son nursery records

common_name: Journey to Oz Daylily (Rose-Red Blend Spider with Wine Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this 2001 Herrington spider-form introduction rewards generous spacing with tall, well-branched scapes.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Journey to Oz is a spider-form daylily bearing large rose-red blend flowers with a wine-red eye above a green throat, held on tall scapes well-branched with numerous buds. Bred by Herrington from Magic of Oz crossed with Red Ribbons, it blooms early to midseason and reblooms, and has placed highly for the AHS Harris Olson Spider Award. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.

common_name: Black Arrowhead Daylily (Mauve-Purple Spider with Plum Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; this 2002 Roberts introduction is a diploid spider type that adapts to a wide range of growing conditions.

directions: Plant in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Black Arrowhead is a whimsical spider-form daylily with large, light mauve-purple flowers accented by a deep plum-purple eye above a green throat that blends to yellow. Introduced by Roberts in 2002 and later given an AHS Honorable Mention, it carries semi-evergreen foliage and has placed highly for the AHS Harris Olson Spider Award. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom size.

common_name: Midnight in Oz Daylily (Burgundy-Red Unusual-Form Rebloomer)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this Herrington introduction, registered in 2009, carries evergreen foliage and reblooms reliably.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Midnight in Oz is an unusual-form spider daylily bearing large, burgundy-red self flowers above a yellow throat, held on scapes around two feet tall. Registered by Herrington in 2009, this diploid rebloomer carries evergreen foliage and has placed highly for the AHS Harris Olson Spider Award. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.

common_name: Ghost Ranger Daylily (Near-White Spider with Green Throat)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this Elliott introduction is a diploid spider/unusual-form type that reblooms late in the season.

directions: Plant in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Ghost Ranger bears huge, near-white spider/unusual-form flowers with a cascading petal twist and a strikingly green throat, carried on tall scapes loaded with buds. Bred by Elliott, this diploid rebloomer flowers late in the season and has placed highly for the AHS Harris Olson Spider Award. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor and bloom count.
